text:
cs-julia: fyi ACME just opened an escalated ticket — p99 embeddings latency up ~3x since last night, also seeing intermittent 401s and a couple of duplicate billing events. customer on eu-west-1, noticed after our maintenance window.
eng-oncall-sam: thanks, forwarding alerts. @infra-joe can you grab host/kernel/driver diffs from last deploy? also any recent CUDA/driver rollouts in eu-west-1?
infra-joe: applying rollouts at 02:00 UTC — CUDA 12.2 -> 13.0 on GPU fleet + NVMe driver 5.12.x bump. no kernel upgrade. rolling patch notes: kernel params unchanged. I have the rollout manifest.
mira-ml: customer workload is embeddings heavy (dense vector writes to kv-cache + disk sharding). high concurrency + small-ish requests. KV cache miss rate jumped ~50% -> increases host IO.
ops-bot: [ALERT] eu-west-1: p99 embeddings latency 2.9s -> 9.1s, error rate 401 up 0.8% -> 4.5%, token refresh errors spiking. Rolling fallback routes active: 10% traffic -> us-west-2.
eng-oncall-sam: curious about 401s — token refresh service shows spikes at same times? Could be auth service timeouts causing retries that amplify load.
sre-ana: grabbing metrics. iostat shows NVMe await distribution widen, qdepth climb during spikes. dmesg tail shows:
```
[Mar 17 02:12:33] nvme nvme0: I/O 12345 timeout, controller reset
[Mar 17 02:12:34] nvme nvme0: removed.
[Mar 17 02:12:34] nvme nvme0: attached. firmware 2.3.7 -> 2.3.9
```
sre-ana: firmware delta noted on some hosts in the window. also seeing a few kernel IO error traces with blk_mq timeouts.
infra-joe: firmware bumps were part of vendor auto-update scheduled during maintenance. that may explain NVMe firmware revs on subset of hosts.
mira-ml: KV cache miss + retry fanout is plausible: auth 401 causes client SDK to attempt refresh -> retry generation -> miss -> disk read for model weights/kv -> higher qdepth -> tail latency.
cs-julia: customer timeline: they reported first at 02:20 UTC, said they saw failed calls and slow responses. asked for ETA and whether we can route them to another region.
eng-oncall-sam: short mitigations: 1) temporarily route customer traffic to us-west-2 (we already have 10% fallback). 2) pause firmware/driver auto-updates in eu-west-1. 3) increase KV cache TTL + warm cache for ACME model. 4) add 401 backoff on SDK to avoid immediate retries.
infra-joe: implementing pause of vendor auto-updates now. patching fleet to pin NVMe firmware and driver to previous version where possible.
sre-ana: while we rollback, recommended quick fix: throttle embeddings concurrency for ACME route (limit concurrent requests) and enable cached-response for recent keys. also bump IO scheduler to deadline on hot nodes.
mira-ml: warming cache: prefetch top 1000 vectors from last 24h for ACME, priming will take ~5m per pod. kicking that off.
eng-oncall-sam: auth team — any visible degradation on token service? @sre-ana can you paste auth logs for a representative pod?
sre-ana: auth pod logs snippet:
```
2026-03-17T02:14:01Z token-service INFO refresh start id=aa3f
2026-03-17T02:14:02Z token-service WARN upstream timeout=1500ms id=aa3f
2026-03-17T02:14:02Z token-service ERROR refresh-failed status=504 id=aa3f
2026-03-17T02:14:03Z client-sdk INFO retrying id=aa3f attempt=1
```
sre-ana: timeouts coincide with NVMe controller resets; suspect storage stalls causing upstream datastore/timeouts for auth, not bug in auth code.
infra-joe: standing up a small pool of unaffected hosts (no firmware bump) and shifting ACME to that pool. deploying route change now.
ops-bot: ACTION: routing change applied for customer ACME -> 100% traffic to eu-west-1-pool-B (hosts pinned to firmware 2.3.7). monitor for 10m.
eng-oncall-sam: CS, tell customer we routed them to a pinned pool and paused auto-updates; we're warming cache and throttling concurrency. ETA for stable fix: 2 hours to finish fleet rollback & verify.
cs-julia: relaying to ACME. they asked whether any billing duplicates will be reversed — investigating.
infra-joe: on duplicate billing: the SDK retries produced duplicate successful completions in a small subset. we'll coordinate with billing to detect duplicate charge IDs and refund. logging trace ids for ACME calls being collected.
mira-ml: repro steps for infra team: (1) deploy CUDA13 + nvme fw 2.3.9 on a host, (2) run high-concurrency embeddings workload with small documents (QPS ~400), (3) induce token-service upstream latency to force 401/refresh retries. Observe p99 spikes and NVMe timeouts.
eng-oncall-sam: please run repro in staging with same hardware profile. infra-joe, can you spin one node with fw 2.3.9 and same driver stack? also capture perf counters: iostat -x 1, pidstat -d, nvidia-smi dmon.
infra-joe: spinning repro node now in staging. will run workload from mira's harness and post logs in this thread.
sre-ana: monitoring: p99 down to 1.2s after routing, 401 rate back under 1%. IO await falling. will keep watch for 30m then mark incident stable.
cs-julia: customer ack'd and said latency improved, still wants a postmortem and refunds for duplicate charges.
eng-oncall-sam: next steps: 1) full rollback plan for NVMe firmware across eu-west-1 (schedule & blast radius). 2) add SDK client-side 401 exponential backoff and idempotency tokens for embeddings calls. 3) add health checks that correlate nvme resets -> route away automatically. 4) billing: run dedupe on ACME trace ids and issue refunds if duplicates exist. assign owners.
infra-joe: owner for rollback: infra-joe. timeline: start 03:30 UTC, expect 1.5h with staggered batches.
mira-ml: owner for SDK/backoff & idempotency: mira-ml + eng-sdk. PR will target next patch, hotfix if necessary.
sre-ana: owner for health-check routing automation: sre-ana + eng-sre.
cs-julia: billing owner: ben-billing (cc). tagging customer for a follow-up call.
eng-oncall-sam: thanks all. keep thread updated with rollback progress and any anomalies. :thumbsup:
